In early 1918 a country that had become independent only weeks earlier split along a line you can see on this map. About 1 in 3 Finns would be involved.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The Finnish Civil War ran from 27 January to 15 May 1918. The Whites fought the Reds, who set up a socialist workers' republic in the south after the war began.
2/ The map shows the geography clearly. Red Finland held the south, including nearly all the major towns and industrial centres. White Finland held the large, rural north.
3/ The turning point was Tampere. The Whites began their assault on 16 March, the fighting in the city began on 28 March, and the Reds surrendered there on 6 April.
4/ Germany joined in on 3 April 1918. Its roughly 10,000-strong Baltic Sea Division landed at Hanko, and the Battle of Helsinki was fought on 12 and 13 April.
5/ Around 38,000 people died in total, most of them on the Red side, roughly 32,000 to 33,000 against about 5,500 for the Whites. The war was short, but it was brutal.
6/ The aftermath was grim. About 12,500 Red prisoners died of malnutrition and disease in camps. Finland's population was about 3.1 million, so the war left a deep, lasting scar.
7/ How did a country that bitterly split in 1918 rebuild its unity? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
